title: Compute-port parity manifest
description: Per-kind declaration consumed by scripts/worker/compare_compute_outputs.py. One manifest fully determines what 'parity' means for one compute kind: how its fixture is produced, which migrations built the stores, what is allowed to vary between two runs, which tables are compared, by which semantic key, and with which per-field numeric policy. There is deliberately no place in this schema for a global float tolerance.

kind.description: Job kind as registered in contracts/jobs/v1/registry.json.

migrations.description: How each store's schema is built. A path, never inline DDL: the comparison is only meaningful against the same migrations the platform ships.

fixture.description: How the input rows are produced. Fixtures are producer-derived: generated by the production fixture generators and written through the production writers, never hand-authored.

source.description: Repo-relative producer that emits the fixture.

command.description: Argv that seeds one destination. Receives PARITY_DSN in the environment.

clone_command.description: Argv that copies the seeded input tables to the second destination so both sides consume byte-identical input.

seed.description: Fixed RNG seed handed to the generator.

digest.description: Recorded digest of a known-good fixture, when one has been pinned. The comparator always recomputes and compares the two sides' input digests regardless of this field.

determinism.description: Every source of run-to-run variation the kind carries, declared rather than discovered. A source that is not listed here and is not canonicalized in outputs[] will surface as a false difference.

producers.description: One entry per implementation, keyed by the side label passed to the comparator (e.g. 'python', 'go').

inputs.description: Tables the kind reads. The comparator validates each side's projection against `fields` and digests the rows with the same type-aware, framed encoding it uses for outputs, then requires the two sides to match BEFORE comparing any output. A mismatch makes the run INDETERMINATE, never DIFFERENT: an output comparison over different inputs is not a parity claim, and an untyped digest would call integer 1 and string "1" the same fixture.

fields.description: Every column the input `select` returns, typed. Projection drift is refused.

select.description: Projection read from each destination. Every selected column must appear in `fields`.

semantic_key.description: Columns that identify a row's meaning. A column canonicalized away by `volatile` may not be a key column: doing so would collapse distinct rows and hide a missing row behind an extra one.

repeat_policy.description: What a second execution over the same input is expected to do to this table. Checked with --repeat 2, per side. 'tombstone' additionally requires tombstone_predicate and asserts that marker rows actually exist after the replay.

tombstone_predicate.description: SQL predicate identifying tombstone rows. REQUIRED when repeat_policy is 'tombstone' and rejected otherwise: the comparator counts matching rows on both sides and after the replay, so the tombstone contract is checked rather than assumed. A producer that deletes nothing and marks nothing fails it.

allow_empty.description: Whether an empty output table on BOTH sides is an acceptable result. Default false: two empty tables have identical counts and identical digests, which is an absence of evidence rather than parity, so the comparator returns INDETERMINATE instead of EQUAL. Set true only for a table a kind may legitimately leave empty, and say why in the manifest's description.

volatile.description: drop: excluded from digest and comparison. placeholder: only null-ness compared. utc_normalize: normalized to UTC then compared exactly. ordinal: compared by the value's rank among the run's own distinct values, for deliberately volatile identifiers.

numeric.description: Per-field numeric comparison. 'exact' is the default posture. A tolerance is only ever declared here, per field, and must carry a written reason naming the persisted column precision that requires it; the comparator refuses a tolerance without one. A tolerance-compared field is excluded from the canonical row digest (a digest is exact by construction) and the report names it under digest_excluded_fields.
